nlq.academic_years.comment: One row is one academic year of the school (school session, e.g. 2026-27, usually April to March). Every year is here: planned (next year being set up), active (the working year), locked and closed (past years). For "this year" filter is_current = true; for "last year" take the year whose end_date is just before the current one's start_date. Other nlq views carry academic_year_id and academic_year (the same code), so join on academic_year_id or filter on academic_year directly. Admission sessions point to the year the children will join, usually the next one.

columns.name: academic_year_id
columns.comment: The year's id; join key to academic_year_id in the other nlq views.

columns.name: academic_year
columns.comment: The year's short code as the school writes it, e.g. 2026-27. The same text appears as academic_year in other nlq views.

columns.name: name
columns.comment: The year's display name, e.g. Session 2026-27.

columns.name: start_date
columns.comment: First day of the academic year.

columns.name: end_date
columns.comment: Last day of the academic year.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: planned (not started, being set up), active (the working year), locked (past year, closed for most changes) or closed (archived past year).

columns.name: is_current
columns.comment: True for exactly one year: the school's working year (status active; the latest-starting one if two are active). False for all others.

nlq.admission_applications.comment: One row is one child's admission application in one admission session (called a registration once it has a registration number), from form submitted to admitted, rejected or cancelled. Left out: drafts (forms started but not submitted) and applications of removed sessions; no names or contact details of the child or family. Admitted means is_admitted = true (status fee_paid or admitted), as the school's admission reports count; in_student_master = the student record is made; ever_admitted also keeps those admitted and cancelled later. Registered = is_registered (registration fee paid or none due). Filter one admission_session (or academic_year, the year the children join, usually next year), group by class (sort class_order), status_label, fee_category or stage. Dates are India dates: group registrations by registered_on, offers by offered_on, admissions by fee_paid_on. Money is rupees: *_paid are receipts actually taken (reversed and bounced left out), refunded = refunds paid out in money, moved_out = money carried to another school of the group. A registration moved to another school shows here as cancelled. Join nlq.admission_enquiries on application_id; nlq.students on student_id for the class-section after admission.

columns.name: application_id
columns.comment: The application's id; join key to nlq.admission_enquiries.application_id.

columns.name: registration_no
columns.comment: The registration number, given when the registration is complete; empty before that (status submitted).

columns.name: cycle_id
columns.comment: The admission session's id.

columns.name: admission_session
columns.comment: The admission session's code, e.g. 2027-28.

columns.name: session_name
columns.comment: The admission session's name, e.g. Admissions 2027-28.

columns.name: academic_year_id
columns.comment: The academic year the children of this session join; join key to nlq.academic_years.

columns.name: academic_year
columns.comment: Code of the year the children join, e.g. 2027-28 (usually the next year).

columns.name: class
columns.comment: The class applied for, e.g. Nursery, I, XI. Sort by class_order.

columns.name: class_order
columns.comment: The class's position for sorting (lower = junior).

columns.name: fee_category
columns.comment: The fee category the form's answers put the child in, e.g. General, EWS, Staff ward, Sibling; empty when not set.

columns.name: gender
columns.comment: The child's gender: male, female, other or unspecified.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: submitted (form in, registration fee due), registered, under_review, sent_back (correction asked of the family), shortlisted, selected (older flow), waitlisted, offered (seat offered, admission fee due; may be part-paid), fee_paid (admission fee paid, admission number given, waiting to be admitted), admitted, rejected (not selected), withdrawn (by the family, or the offer lapsed unpaid), cancelled (by the school, moved to another school, or the admission cancelled later).

columns.name: status_label
columns.comment: The status in the words of the admission lists: Registration fee due, Registered, Under review, Correction asked, Shortlisted, Selected, Waiting list, Offered, Admission fee paid, Admitted, Not selected, Withdrawn, Cancelled.

columns.name: stage
columns.comment: For a registration in the approval process, the stage it waits at, e.g. Document check, Written test, Interview, Selection; empty otherwise.

columns.name: level_no
columns.comment: The approval level it waits at within that stage (1 = first); empty when not waiting.

columns.name: waiting_since_on
columns.comment: Date it reached its current stage and level (India date); days waiting = current_date - waiting_since_on.

columns.name: is_registered
columns.comment: True when a registration number was given (registration complete).

columns.name: is_in_process
columns.comment: True while in the approval process: registered, under_review, sent_back or shortlisted.

columns.name: is_selected
columns.comment: True when selected, on the waiting list or offered a seat (not yet paid).

columns.name: is_admitted
columns.comment: True when admitted as the admission reports count it: admission fee paid (fee_paid) or admitted.

columns.name: in_student_master
columns.comment: True when the student record has been made (status admitted).

columns.name: ever_admitted
columns.comment: True when a student record was made from it at some time, even if the admission was cancelled later.

columns.name: is_closed
columns.comment: True when closed without admission: rejected, withdrawn or cancelled.

columns.name: online_form
columns.comment: True for applications made on the school's admission forms (the current process); false for the older first-version flow. The admission lists show only true.

columns.name: entered_at_desk
columns.comment: True when the office filled the form at the desk for a walk-in family.

columns.name: possible_duplicate
columns.comment: True when the same child may have applied twice in the session (flagged, not removed).

columns.name: started_on
columns.comment: Date the form was started (India date).

columns.name: submitted_on
columns.comment: Date the form was submitted (India date).

columns.name: registered_on
columns.comment: Date the registration was completed and numbered (India date); empty before.

columns.name: month
columns.comment: First day of the month of registered_on (or submitted_on when not registered); group by it for month-wise registrations.

columns.name: offered_on
columns.comment: Date a seat was offered (India date); empty when not offered.

columns.name: offer_expires_on
columns.comment: Last date to pay the admission fee for the offer (India date).

columns.name: fee_paid_on
columns.comment: Date the admission fee was fully paid and the admission number given (India date).

columns.name: admitted_on
columns.comment: Date the child was admitted into the student records (India date); empty for older-flow admissions, use in_student_master.

columns.name: cancelled_on
columns.comment: Date the application was cancelled (India date).

columns.name: registration_fee
columns.comment: Registration fee asked of this application (rupees), by class and fee category.

columns.name: admission_fee
columns.comment: Admission fee asked with the offer (rupees); empty before an offer.

columns.name: registration_fee_paid
columns.comment: Registration fee actually received (rupees): posted receipts; reversed and bounced left out.

columns.name: admission_fee_paid
columns.comment: Admission fee actually received so far (rupees): posted receipts, part payments added up; reversed and bounced left out.

columns.name: refunded
columns.comment: Money refunded and paid out to the family (rupees), after the school's deduction.

columns.name: moved_out
columns.comment: Money carried to another school of the group when the registration was moved there (rupees; no cash paid out).

columns.name: transfer_credit
columns.comment: Money brought in from another school of the group not yet used against the admission fee (rupees).

columns.name: form_points
columns.comment: Merit points from the form's answers (sibling, alumni, distance and similar criteria).

columns.name: merit
columns.comment: Merit total used to rank: form points plus test and interview marks; higher ranks first.

columns.name: wait_rank
columns.comment: Position on the waiting list (1 = next); empty when not waiting.

columns.name: admission_no
columns.comment: The admission number given when the admission fee was paid; empty before. Never given again, even if cancelled.

columns.name: student_id
columns.comment: The student record made at admission; join key to nlq.students. Empty before admission.

nlq.admission_enquiries.comment: One row is one admission enquiry (a lead): a family asking about admission by walk-in, call, the website or a campaign, with its source, class asked for, stage on the enquiry board, counsellor, follow-up dates, and whether the family registered and was admitted. Every enquiry is here, open or closed; no personal details of the family or child are. Funnel: enquiries -> stage_kind started (registration form begun) -> is_registered (registration completed, registration number given; status converted) -> is_admitted (admission fee paid or admitted, as the school's enquiry report counts). Lost = is_lost (not interested or closed). Filter by enquired_on (or month) for enquiries taken in a period, or by admission_session / academic_year (the year the child would join). Group by source, class (sort class_order), counsellor, stage or score. For the registration itself join nlq.admission_applications on application_id.

columns.name: enquiry_id
columns.comment: The enquiry's id (the enquiry number the family is told).

columns.name: enquired_on
columns.comment: Date the enquiry was taken (India date).

columns.name: month
columns.comment: First day of the month of enquired_on; group by it for month-wise counts.

columns.name: cycle_id
columns.comment: The admission session the enquiry is for; join key to cycle_id in nlq.admission_applications. Empty when not given.

columns.name: admission_session
columns.comment: The admission session's code, e.g. 2027-28 (admissions for that joining year); empty when not given.

columns.name: academic_year_id
columns.comment: The academic year the child would join (the session's year); join key to nlq.academic_years.

columns.name: academic_year
columns.comment: Code of the year the child would join, e.g. 2027-28 (usually next year, not the year the enquiry was taken).

columns.name: class
columns.comment: The class asked for, e.g. Nursery, I, XI; empty when not given. Sort by class_order.

columns.name: class_order
columns.comment: The class's position for sorting (lower = junior).

columns.name: source
columns.comment: Where the enquiry came from, as the school names its sources (e.g. Website, Walk-in, Newspaper, Reference); Not given when empty.

columns.name: campaign
columns.comment: The campaign named on the enquiry, if any (e.g. a fair or an advertisement).

columns.name: from_website
columns.comment: True when the family filled the enquiry form on the school's website.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: new, follow_up, interested (all three open), converted (the family completed a registration), not_interested or closed (both lost).

columns.name: stage
columns.comment: The stage on the school's enquiry board, e.g. New, Contacted, Interested, Campus visit, Registration started, Registered, Admitted, Lost (the school may rename or add stages).

columns.name: stage_kind
columns.comment: What the stage means: open (being worked), started (registration form begun), registered, admitted or lost.

columns.name: is_open
columns.comment: True while the enquiry is being worked (status new, follow_up or interested).

columns.name: is_lost
columns.comment: True when the enquiry was lost (status not_interested or closed).

columns.name: is_registered
columns.comment: True when the family completed a registration from this enquiry (registration number given; the enquiry is then converted). A registration begun but not completed shows only as stage_kind started.

columns.name: is_admitted
columns.comment: True when the child was admitted from it: the application's admission fee is paid or the child is admitted (the enquiry report's rule).

columns.name: score
columns.comment: How warm the lead is: hot, warm or cold; empty when not rated.

columns.name: counsellor
columns.comment: Name of the counsellor the enquiry is assigned to; empty when unassigned.

columns.name: is_escalated
columns.comment: True when the first contact was not made in time and the enquiry moved to the second level (a senior person).

columns.name: next_follow_up_on
columns.comment: Date of the next follow-up planned; empty when none.

columns.name: follow_up_overdue
columns.comment: True when the enquiry is open and its next follow-up date has passed.

columns.name: first_contact_on
columns.comment: Date of the first call, visit, message, reply or invitation to the family (India date); empty when not yet contacted.

columns.name: hours_to_first_contact
columns.comment: Hours from the enquiry to the first contact (number, one decimal; clock hours, not working hours); empty when not yet contacted.

columns.name: first_contact_late
columns.comment: True when the enquiry is open, not yet contacted, and the time the assignment rule allows for the first contact has passed.

columns.name: last_contact_on
columns.comment: Date of the latest contact with the family (India date).

columns.name: contacts
columns.comment: Number of contacts made (calls, visits, e-mails, SMS, WhatsApp, replies, invitations); notes and system entries are not counted.

columns.name: converted_on
columns.comment: Date the family registered from this enquiry (India date); empty when not converted.

columns.name: application_id
columns.comment: The registration started from this enquiry; join key to nlq.admission_applications. Empty when none.

columns.name: registration_no
columns.comment: The registration number of that application, once registered.

nlq.assets.comment: One row is one unit of an asset item in the asset register (one tag: a laptop, a projector, a lab microscope). All assets are listed, also those that have left the books; filter is_on_books for the register as it stands (in store, in use, in transit, under repair, lost). Money in rupees. book_value is the closing value of the latest financial year for which depreciation was run (book_value_year), else the cost: it does not fall between yearly runs. Use: count or sum cost / book_value by category, department, store or status; who holds what = employee_name (the custodian). An asset item kept in a store is also counted in nlq.stock_balances, so do not add asset values to stock values. Join nlq.staff on employee_id for the custodian department or whether they still work here.

columns.name: asset_id
columns.comment: Id of the asset.

columns.name: asset_code
columns.comment: Asset tag printed on its label, e.g. AST/2026-27/0031 or an old register tag.

columns.name: item_id
columns.comment: Id of the catalogue item it is a unit of.

columns.name: item_code
columns.comment: Item code, e.g. IT-LAP-0002.

columns.name: item
columns.comment: Item name, e.g. Laptop.

columns.name: category
columns.comment: Main item category, e.g. IT equipment (depreciation is set per main category).

columns.name: sub_category
columns.comment: Item sub-category; empty when none.

columns.name: make
columns.comment: Make (brand) of the unit.

columns.name: model
columns.comment: Model of the unit.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: in_store, in_use (issued to a department or person), in_transit (between stores), under_repair, lost, returned (sent back to the vendor), written_off (condemned), disposed (condemned and sold, scrapped or given away).

columns.name: is_on_books
columns.comment: True while the school still holds it: status in_store, in_use, in_transit, under_repair or lost.

columns.name: condition
columns.comment: good, fair, poor or unserviceable.

columns.name: store_id
columns.comment: Id of the store it is kept in (when in store).

columns.name: store
columns.comment: Store it is kept in; empty when it is out in use.

columns.name: department_id
columns.comment: Id of the department that holds it.

columns.name: department
columns.comment: Department that holds it; empty while in store.

columns.name: location
columns.comment: Room or place where it is, as typed (e.g. Computer lab 2).

columns.name: employee_id
columns.comment: Id of the custodian (the employee it is handed to); join key to nlq.staff.employee_id.

columns.name: employee_code
columns.comment: Employee code of the custodian.

columns.name: employee_name
columns.comment: Name of the custodian; empty when nobody holds it personally.

columns.name: source
columns.comment: How it came on the register: Goods receipt (bought through a PO), Opening stock, or Imported or added by hand (an old register).

columns.name: vendor_id
columns.comment: Id of the vendor it was bought from.

columns.name: vendor
columns.comment: Vendor it was bought from; empty when not known.

columns.name: po_no

columns.name: bought_on
columns.comment: Date acquired (else the day put to use, else the day it was registered).

columns.name: put_to_use_on
columns.comment: Date put to use (depreciation runs from it); empty when not recorded.

columns.name: cost
columns.comment: Cost of the unit in rupees: its share of the PO line with GST and charges, or the opening rate.

columns.name: book_value
columns.comment: Written-down value in rupees at the end of book_value_year (the latest depreciation run), else cost.

columns.name: depreciation_to_date
columns.comment: cost less book_value, in rupees: depreciation charged in the runs so far.

columns.name: book_value_year
columns.comment: Financial year (e.g. 2025-26) whose closing value book_value is; empty when no depreciation has been run.

columns.name: warranty_until

columns.name: insured_value
columns.comment: Insured value in rupees; empty when not insured.

columns.name: insurance_renewal
columns.comment: Date the insurance is due for renewal.

columns.name: left_on

columns.name: book_value_at_exit

nlq.attendance_days.comment: One row is one pupil's mark in the class's day register on one school day (the daily attendance the class teacher takes; subject-period attendance is not here). Only days with a register appear: holidays and weekly offs have no rows, and a pupil the teacher did not mark has no row that day (not marked is not absent). Left out: removed, merged or erased student records, pupils whose admission that year was cancelled, and marks of old closed years the school has archived. Counting rule (the register's own): days = rows; present = is_present (every code except A absent and LV leave; late, half day, short leave, on duty and stay back count as present, a half day as a whole day); attendance % = 100 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_present) / count(*), so leave lowers the %. For % without leave days use count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_leave) as the base, and say so. Filter on on_date (a date range is fastest; month is for grouping) and academic_year; group by class_section, class (sort class_order) or student. class / section are those of the register the mark is in (the pupil's section that day). Join nlq.students on student_id and academic_year_id for gender, category or house.

columns.name: student_id
columns.comment: The pupil's id; join key to nlq.students (with academic_year_id).

columns.name: admission_no
columns.comment: The pupil's admission number.

columns.name: student_name
columns.comment: The pupil's full name.

columns.name: academic_year_id
columns.comment: The academic year of the register; join key to nlq.academic_years.

columns.name: academic_year
columns.comment: The academic year code, e.g. 2026-27.

columns.name: class
columns.comment: The class of the register, e.g. VI. Sort by class_order.

columns.name: class_order
columns.comment: The class's position for sorting (lower = junior).

columns.name: section
columns.comment: The section of the register, e.g. A.

columns.name: class_section
columns.comment: Class and section of the register, e.g. VI-A.

columns.name: class_section_id
columns.comment: The class-section's id; join key to nlq.class_sections and nlq.section_attendance.

columns.name: on_date
columns.comment: The school day (India date).

columns.name: month
columns.comment: First day of the month of on_date; group by it for month-wise attendance.

columns.name: code
columns.comment: The register code: P present, A absent, L late, SR short leave (left early), H half day, OD on duty, SB stay back, LV on approved leave.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: The code in words: present, absent, late, short_leave, half_day, on_duty, stay_back or leave.

columns.name: is_present
columns.comment: True when the pupil counts as present that day (every code except A and LV). Use count(*) FILTER (WHERE is_present) for present days.

columns.name: is_absent
columns.comment: True when marked absent (code A).

columns.name: is_leave
columns.comment: True when on approved leave (code LV); neither present nor absent, but still a day of the register.

columns.name: is_late
columns.comment: True when marked late (code L); a late pupil is also present.

columns.name: source
columns.comment: How the mark was made: manual (by the teacher), rfid (gate card reader) or upload (an Excel list).

columns.name: gate_in_time
columns.comment: India time the pupil's card was first read at the gate that day (RFID schools); empty otherwise.

columns.name: gate_out_time
columns.comment: India time of the last gate exit read that day (RFID schools); empty otherwise.

nlq.certificates.comment: One row is one certificate paper in the certificate register: an original (copy_no 0) or a duplicate of it (same number, copy_no 1, 2 ...), for a student or a staff member: transfer certificate (type_code TC), bonafide, character, date of birth, fee paid, award certificates, experience and others. Every TC is here (use this view, not any other TC list). Cancelled papers are kept (status cancelled). Use: certificates issued = count rows WHERE copy_no = 0 (originals); valid now = is_valid; duplicates = is_duplicate. Group by type, month (of issued_on) or academic_year. academic_year is the year recorded on the certificate (the year the office was working in), which can differ from the year of issued_on around April. The class is the student enrolment in that academic year. A re-issue cancels the old paper and gives a new number (is_reissue, reissued_as_number); a correction keeping the number raises revision and moves issued_on to the correction day (first_issued_on keeps the first). is_old_system rows came from the previous software. The printed details of the paper are not available here.

columns.name: certificate_id
columns.comment: Id of the certificate paper.

columns.name: type_code
columns.comment: Code of the certificate type: TC, BONAFIDE, CHARACTER, DOB, DOB_JUST, STUDY, CASTE, DOMICILE, NOC, TRAVEL_NOC, VISA, SCHOLAR, BOARD_REG, BOARD_FORM, FEE_PAID, ACHIEVEMENT, MERIT, PARTICIPATION, AWARD (students), EXPERIENCE, SERVICE, STAFF_VISA (staff), or a code the school made.

columns.name: type
columns.comment: Name of the certificate type, e.g. Transfer certificate, Bonafide certificate.

columns.name: audience
columns.comment: student or staff: who the type is for.

columns.name: number
columns.comment: Certificate number, e.g. TC/2026-27/00012; a duplicate repeats the number of its original.

columns.name: copy_no
columns.comment: 0 for the original, 1, 2 ... for each duplicate of it.

columns.name: is_duplicate
columns.comment: True for a duplicate (copy_no above 0). Count duplicates apart from certificates issued.

columns.name: original_id
columns.comment: For a duplicate, the certificate_id of its original; empty for an original.

columns.name: status
columns.comment: issued or cancelled. Cancelling an original cancels its duplicates too.

columns.name: is_valid
columns.comment: True for an original (copy_no 0) that is still issued (not cancelled). Count these for valid certificates.

columns.name: issued_on
columns.comment: Date of issue (for a corrected certificate, the date of its latest correction; for a duplicate, the day the duplicate was made). Filter periods on this date.

columns.name: month
columns.comment: First day of the month of issued_on.

columns.name: first_issued_on
columns.comment: Date the certificate was first issued, before any correction.

columns.name: cancelled_on
columns.comment: Date it was cancelled (India time); empty when not cancelled.

columns.name: academic_year
columns.comment: Academic year code recorded on the certificate, e.g. 2026-27 (also the middle part of its number).

columns.name: academic_year_id
columns.comment: Id of that academic year; join key to nlq.academic_years and nlq.students.

columns.name: book_no
columns.comment: TC book number (100 TCs to a book); empty for other types.

columns.name: sl_no
columns.comment: Serial number in the TC book series (runs on across books and years); empty for other types.

columns.name: revision
columns.comment: 1 for a certificate as issued; 2, 3 ... after each correction that kept the number.

columns.name: is_corrected
columns.comment: True when the certificate was corrected under the same number (revision above 1).

columns.name: is_reissue
columns.comment: True when this certificate re-issued an earlier one (which was cancelled then).

columns.name: reissue_of_number
columns.comment: Number of the cancelled certificate this one re-issued; empty otherwise.

columns.name: reissued_as_number
columns.comment: Number of the new certificate that re-issued this one; empty otherwise.

columns.name: is_override
columns.comment: True when it was issued although one of its checks failed (fees due, books out ...), on the principal override.

columns.name: is_old_system
columns.comment: True for a certificate brought from the previous software (read-only history, old number).

columns.name: requested_via
columns.comment: parent, student or staff when it answered a request made in an app, office when the office entered the request, direct when issued without a request.

columns.name: is_bulk
columns.comment: True when it was issued in a bulk run (a whole section, leavers, awards, an Excel sheet).

columns.name: student_id
columns.comment: Id of the student (empty for a staff certificate); join key to nlq.students.student_id.

columns.name: admission_no
columns.comment: Admission number of the student.

columns.name: student_name
columns.comment: Name of the student as on the student record now.

columns.name: class
columns.comment: Class of the student in academic_year (from that year enrolment); empty when none.

columns.name: class_order
columns.comment: Display order of the class, for sorting.

columns.name: section
columns.comment: Section of the student in academic_year.

columns.name: class_section
columns.comment: Class and section, e.g. X-A.

columns.name: class_section_id
columns.comment: Id of the class section; join key to nlq.class_sections.

columns.name: employee_id
columns.comment: Id of the staff member (empty for a student certificate); join key to nlq.staff.employee_id.

columns.name: employee_code
columns.comment: Employee code of the staff member.

columns.name: employee_name
columns.comment: Name of the staff member.

columns.name: person_name
columns.comment: Name of the student or staff member it is for.

columns.name: issued_by
columns.comment: Staff name of the person who issued it; empty when not known.

nlq.class_sections.comment: One row is one class-section (e.g. VI-A) of one academic year, with its class teacher and number of pupils. Sections are per year: VI-A of 2025-26 and VI-A of 2026-27 are two rows, so filter is_current_year = true (or one academic_year) first. Removed sections are left out. strength counts pupils the way the school's strength reports do: for the current or a future year, pupils whose enrolment is active now; for a year already over, pupils on the section's roll on the year's last day. Cancelled admissions and removed or merged student records never count. Sum strength by class for class strength (sort by class_order). For pupil-level detail use nlq.students on class_section_id.

columns.name: class_section_id
columns.comment: The class-section's id (one per year); join key to class_section_id in nlq.students and other views.

columns.name: academic_year_id
columns.comment: The academic year this section belongs to; join key to nlq.academic_years.

columns.name: academic_year

nlq.exam_marks.comment: One row is one pupil's paper (subject) in one exam: pupil × exam × subject, for every paper the pupil takes, whether marks are entered yet or not (is_entered). Left out: deleted exams, deleted, merged or erased pupils, cancelled enrolments; a pupil who left the school, and an exam set up without a marks area (indicators or remarks only), keep only the papers that have an entry. Marks are the raw entries of the marks sheets: they include sheets still open or only submitted — for official (final) figures keep is_verified = true. A paper holds marks, or a code instead of marks (AB absent, ML medical leave, EX exempted, NA, OD, L, NEW ADM …), or a grade (grade-only papers, max_marks = 0). For averages use percent or marks (codes are empty there); for totals as the exam result counts them use marks_counted where counts_in_total. Filter by exam_code / exam_name and academic_year; group by class, class_section or subject_name (sort by class_order, subject_order). Join nlq.exam_results on (student_id, exam_id) for the pupil's overall result, nlq.students on (student_id, academic_year_id) for gender, category, house.

nlq.exam_results.comment: One row is one pupil's overall result in one exam (pupil × exam): total, maximum, percent, grade, pass / fail and rank. These are the stored results EduPro works out from the marks each time a marks sheet is verified or reopened (or the office presses Compute): they reflect the last compute, not marks typed since (computed_on tells when). A pupil enrolled after the last compute has no row yet. Only pupils who were in the class when it was computed are here; left out: deleted exams, deleted, merged or erased pupils, cancelled enrolments. The total counts compulsory and optional marks papers only (additional subjects and grade-only papers stay out; AB counts 0; ML, EX, NA, OD and similar codes take the paper out of the maximum). result: pass, fail (failed a paper: below pass marks or AB) or incomplete (a paper still has no entry: no rank). For pass % use result IN ('pass','fail') as the base, not incomplete rows. Ranks are dense (1, 2, 2, 3) by percent. Filter by exam_code / exam_name and academic_year; group by class (sort by class_order) or class_section. Join nlq.exam_marks on (student_id, exam_id) for the papers, nlq.students on (student_id, academic_year_id) for gender, category, house.

nlq.fee_bills.comment: One row is one bill line of a pupil: one fee head (Tuition, Transport, Previous dues, Bounce charge ...) for one fee month of one academic year, on the school ledger or the hostel ledger. This is what the school asks the family to pay and what has been paid against it. Left out: lines taken off the bill (cancelled: months after a pupil left, hostel months not stayed), old-year lines carried into the next year's opening balance (carried; the same money is on the new year's Previous dues lines), removed and merged duplicate pupils. The LATE FEE IS NOT IN THIS VIEW: it is worked out live from the day of payment and is not a bill line until collected (collected late fee is in nlq.fee_receipts.late_fee); only last year's unpaid late fine, carried forward, appears here as head_kind late_fee. Dues / outstanding = sum(balance); billed = sum(net); concession = sum(concession). Filter one academic_year first. For "overdue" use is_overdue or due_on < a date; for "dues of a month" group by fee_month (the month billed) or due_month (the month the last date falls in; a quarterly plan puts three fee months on one due date). balance can be negative on an opening advance (credit) line, which correctly lowers the pupil's total. paid on a single line can be overstated when an opening credit sits in the same instalment, so for money collected per head use nlq.fee_receipt_heads; per pupil, class or month sum(paid) is right. School and hostel are mixed unless you filter ledger. Join nlq.students on student_id + academic_year_id.

nlq.fee_concessions.comment: One row is one bill line (a pupil's fee head for one fee month of one academic year) that has something taken off it. concession is the whole amount taken off; it is split into waived (fee waivers approved for this line and not taken back) and other_concession (concession types such as sibling or staff ward, refunds where the fee was cancelled, write-off of months after a withdrawal, a paid bounce charge or late fee moved into fee, and rounding to whole rupees). The bills do not record which concession type gave each rupee: discount_types lists the types the pupil holds now for that month and head, so group by discount_types for "concession by type" knowing that a line with two types shows both names together. Left out: lines not billed now (cancelled, carried), removed and merged pupils; lines with nothing taken off. Totals: sum(concession), sum(waived). Filter one academic_year; group by class, head, fee_month, ledger, discount_types or fee_group. Join nlq.fee_bills on bill_line_id for paid and balance.

nlq.fee_receipt_heads.comment: One row is the part of one fee receipt set against one fee head for one fee month (line_kind fee), plus one row for the late fee collected on the receipt (line_kind late_fee) and one for money not yet set against any bill (line_kind advance). The rows of a receipt add up to its amount minus what was refunded from it (a refund takes the money off the head it came from), so per receipt sum(amount) = nlq.fee_receipts.net_amount. Figures are what the receipts are set against today. Filter received_on or month for money received in a period (the receipt date); fee_month tells which month's fee the money paid. Group by head, head_kind, ledger, class or month. Join nlq.fee_receipts on receipt_id for receipt details.

nlq.fee_receipts.comment: One row is one fee receipt of a pupil (school fee or hostel fee) that counts as money received: at the counter, from an Excel upload, or paid online. Left out: cancelled receipts (reversed, never counted) and bounced cheques (the money never came), removed and merged duplicate pupils. Misc fees, admission and registration fees are not here (nlq.misc_receipts). Money collected = sum(amount) filtered on received_on (the receipt date, India) or month; amount = fee_part + late_fee and holds any advance; refunds are NOT taken off amount: subtract sum(nlq.fee_refunds.amount) by its paid_on for "net of refunds" by date, or use net_amount (amount - refunded) for the receipt as it stands today. Filter by received_on / month for "collected in a period", never by academic_year (that is the year of the bills the receipt settles: April receipts often pay last year's dues). Class and section are the pupil's in that academic year (as in the school's day book). Group by mode_name, ledger, class, received_by or month. Head-wise split of the money: nlq.fee_receipt_heads (join on receipt_id).

nlq.helpdesk_queries.comment: One row is one helpdesk ticket: a parent's query or complaint about a pupil (desk parent), a staff query (staff), a ticket to the ERP provider (provider), a hostel complaint (hostel) or an admission family's question (candidate). The old family leave requests stored with them are left out (leave is in the attendance views). No subject, text or reply is here. Always say which desk: filter desk = 'parent' for parent queries and complaints. Open work: is_open (anything not closed; answered is not closed); overdue: open or in progress past its due time now. Group by month (of opened_on), desk, head, status, class or class_section. Speed: avg(hours_to_first_response), avg(hours_to_close) — clock hours, not working hours. The app's "within SLA" share = count(*) FILTER (WHERE closed_within_sla) / count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'closed'). Pupil columns are filled for parent tickets (and hostel ones a parent raised); join nlq.students on student_id and academic_year_id for more about the pupil; employee columns are the staff member who raised a staff ticket.

Boarders on a past day D: from_date <= D AND (to_date IS NULL OR to_date >= D). Boarders in a month: from_date <= the last day AND (to_date IS NULL OR to_date >= the first day). Left the hostel in a period: ended_by IN ('left_hostel', 'left_school') and to_date in the period. Removed and merged pupil records are left out. Class and section are those of the academic year containing the stay's latest day so far (today for a current stay). The hostel fee is billed in the fee views (ledger hostel), not here. nlq.library_loans.comment: One row is one issue of one library copy (a book) to a pupil or a staff member, from issue to return. Issues in a period: filter issued_on; returns: is_returned = true and returned_on in the period (a lost book also closes its loan but is_returned is false and is_lost true). Readers: count(DISTINCT student_id) for pupils, count(DISTINCT employee_id) for staff. Fines are only those sent to the fees counter (from Oct 2026): late_fine is the fine owed after any reduction, late_fine_paid what was paid, late_fine_due what is still owed; older fines kept only at the library are not shown. book_charge is what a lost or damaged book was charged. All money in rupees. Class and section are the pupil's in the academic year containing issued_on; empty for staff. Removed and merged borrower records are left out. Join nlq.library_copies on copy_id.

nlq.messages.comment: One row is one outgoing message from the school: one address on one channel (SMS, WhatsApp, e-mail) or one app push to one phone or browser (a person with two phones gets two push rows). It holds every message the ERP sends, not only bulk circulars: automatic alerts (attendance, fees, transport, gate pass…), one-time sign-in codes, helpdesk and visitor e-mails, payslip and order e-mails. Cancelled messages are left out. No address, recipient or text is here. For "how did our messages do": count rows, count(*) FILTER (WHERE went_out) and FILTER (WHERE delivered), FILTER (WHERE failed). Delivery receipts come only for SMS through MSG91 and WhatsApp through Meta; e-mail, push and the other gateways stay "sent" for ever, so judge them by went_out and failed, never by delivered. Group by created_on or month (India dates), channel, kind, template_name; filter kind = 'bulk send' for circulars composed in Communication, and use request_id / request_title to look at one circular (each person counts once per channel). Usage: sum(units) of rows with went_out; cost_estimate in rupees. Most dashboards leave push out (channel <> 'push').

columns.name: channel

columns.name: status
columns.comment: waiting (queued or being sent; also messages scheduled for later), sent (the gateway accepted it; no delivery receipt), delivered (a delivery receipt confirmed it), failed (the gateway refused it or reported failure after the last retry).

columns.name: went_out
columns.comment: True when the message left the school: status sent or delivered. Use this as "sent" in reports.

columns.name: delivered

columns.name: failed
columns.comment: True when the message failed.

columns.name: read_on_whatsapp

columns.name: kind
columns.comment: What sent it: bulk send (a circular composed in Communication → Compose), one-time code (sign-in or verification code), app push, helpdesk mail (escalation e-mails), visitor mail (telling staff a visitor came), alert (an automatic message from a template: attendance, fees, transport, gate pass, clinic, appointments…), test e-mail, other mail (system e-mails without a template: payslips, purchase orders, letters).

columns.name: sender_name

columns.name: units

columns.name: cost_estimate

Misc fees are separate from the regular school and hostel fee (nlq.fee_bills). Left out: misc fees not yet approved or rejected, lines cancelled, removed and merged pupils, removed staff. paid is net of cancelled, bounced and refunded misc receipts. For "who still owes" filter status = 'open' AND NOT is_closed (an optional fee past its last date is not asked for any more); "overdue" = is_overdue. Totals per fee: count(*), sum(amount) billed, sum(paid) collected, sum(balance). Filter academic_year or misc_fee; staff lines have payer_type staff and no class. nlq.misc_receipts.comment: One row is one misc receipt that stands: money for an announced misc fee (trip, exam form, library charge ...), a registration or admission fee of a new applicant, or other income (from pupils, staff, vendors or others). Regular school and hostel fee receipts are not here (nlq.fee_receipts). Left out: cancelled (reversed) and bounced misc receipts, receipts of removed and merged pupils. amount is what was received on received_on; refunded is what was later given back (misc refunds are not dated here); net_amount = amount - refunded is what the school keeps. For "money received in a period" sum(amount) by received_on or month; for "income kept" sum(net_amount). Group by purpose, head, misc_fee, mode_name or month. Mode transfer is money moved in from another school of the group, not cash. Payers who are not pupils or staff (parents, vendors, applicants) are not named. nlq.payslip_lines.comment: One row is one pay head on one employee's salary for one pay month: e.g. Basic Pay, Dearness Allowance, HRA, Provident Fund, Income Tax (TDS), Advance Recovery — the amounts of every pay run of that month (regular, supplementary, bonus, full and final) added together. Heads that come to 0 are left out. The small net-pay rounding adjustment is its own row (pay_head 'Rounding', category ROUNDING, a deduction that can be negative). Same scope as nlq.payslips: approved, locked or paid runs only; failed records, deleted runs, the go-live's trial runs and confidential staff left out. Final figures: is_final = true. Earnings minus deductions of an employee-month = nlq.payslips.net_pay; earnings summed = gross_pay. Employer contributions (school's PF / ESI share) are NOT lines — they are in nlq.payslips. Group by pay_head (or pay_head_code) and kind; filter month (first day of the pay month) or financial_year (April to March). Amounts are rupees, deductions positive. Join nlq.payslips on (employee_id, month), nlq.staff on employee_id.

Schools add their own.

nlq.payslips.comment: One row is one employee's salary for one pay month: every pay run of that month (the regular run plus any supplementary, bonus or full-and-final run) added together, so an employee appears once per month. Only runs that were approved, locked or paid count; failed records, deleted runs, the trial runs EduPro made while the school was still moving from its old payroll, and the staff the payroll admin marked confidential are left out. Final figures: filter is_final = true (approved-only months are PROVISIONAL and can still change). Money actually paid: is_paid = true. Group by month (first day of the pay month) or financial_year (April to March, e.g. 2026-27) — never by academic year; paid_on is when the money went, not the month it is for. Amounts are rupees. gross_pay - total_deductions = net_pay. Count people with count(*) (one row per person per month). Department, designation and staff_group are as on the payslip of that month (not today's). Join nlq.payslip_lines on (employee_id, month) for head-by-head amounts, and nlq.staff on employee_id for today's details. Bank details, PAN, UAN and ESI numbers are not here.

columns.name: gross_pay

columns.name: total_deductions

columns.name: net_pay
columns.comment: Take-home salary for the month (rupees) = gross_pay - total_deductions.

columns.name: tds

columns.name: profession_tax

Use: sum total for spend (rupees, with GST, rounded to the rupee); group by department, vendor, month or financial_year; filter on po_date (the order date). The year is the Indian financial year April to March (financial_year like 2026-27), not the academic year. total includes freight and other charges and leaves out reverse_charge_gst. nlq.section_attendance.comment: One row is one class-section's day register (daily attendance) taken on one school day, with its counts. Counted live from the registers (not from the 15-minute summary), by the register's own rule: present = every code except A (absent) and LV (approved leave), so late, half day, short leave, on duty and stay back are present; leave is counted apart in on_leave. Only registers that were taken appear: a section with no row on a working day has not marked its attendance (compare with nlq.class_sections of the current year), and holidays have no rows. Subject-period attendance is not here. Marks of removed, merged or erased student records and of cancelled admissions are left out. For a class or the school, add the counts and work the % from the sums: 100 * sum(present) / sum(marked); never average present_pct. Filter on on_date (a date range is fastest; month is for grouping). For pupil-level questions use nlq.attendance_days.

columns.name: marked_late

Removed records and people erased for data protection are left out; leavers stay (status inactive, left_on set). For "how many staff do we have" filter is_current = true. Group by department, designation, staff_type (the finer type such as Teaching Regular) or staff_group (teaching / non_teaching / contract / visiting). Department and designation are today's values on the employee record (no history). Join other staff views on employee_id. A person moved to a sister school appears there as a new employee; here they show left_on = the transfer date.

nlq.staff_attendance_days.comment: One row is one employee's attendance day as the school's staff attendance register shows it (staff, not pupils). A day with NO row is "not marked" (not worked out yet) and must never be counted as absent; today and future days usually have no row. Filter attendance_date (or month) for the period. Sum present_days for days present (half days count 0.5); count is_absent for absences; Attendance % = 100 * (sum(present_days) + sum(paid_leave_days)) / working days, working days = count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_off_day) (the school's reports also count past days not marked as working days, so their % can be lower). To match the school's reports add counted_in_reports = true (staff on the "Not required" list are false). Leave the system charged for late marks or missing punches does NOT change the day (it stays present): for leave and loss-of-pay totals use nlq.staff_leave_days. Join to nlq.staff on employee_id.

nlq.staff_leave_balances.comment: One row is the leave ledger of one employee × leave type × month, for leave types that keep a balance (e.g. CL, EL, SL, HPL, CO; on duty, maternity and loss of pay have none). The balance now = the row with is_latest = true (the month-end job opens the current month every night; a type with no row has no balance). balance is the closing once the month is closed, else opening + credited + correction − used. used = days of leave RAISED in that month (pending or approved, whatever the leave's dates), so it is not "leave taken in that month": for leave taken in a period use nlq.staff_leave_days. Do not add balances across months (each month carries the last). Days lapse only in the leave-session's last month (usually March). Join to nlq.staff on employee_id.

nlq.staff_leave_days.comment: One row is one approved day (or half day) of staff leave: employee × day × leave application. Pending, rejected, withdrawn and cancelled leave and days cut off a shortened leave are left out; leave the system charged (for late marks, missing punches, absence) is included. Days taken = sum(days) (a half day is 0.5) — never count rows. Filter leave_date / month / financial_year (the leave year runs April to March). Weekly offs and holidays charged by the sandwich rule are rows too; for working days lost add is_working_day = true. On duty and work from home (counts_as_present) are leave types but the person was working: leave them out of "absent on leave" questions. A day may have two rows (two half days). One application = one leave_number; a leave split for a short balance has a paid part and a loss-of-pay part with different numbers. To match the school's reports add counted_in_reports = true. Join to nlq.staff on employee_id; to nlq.staff_attendance_days on (employee_id, leave_date = attendance_date).

nlq.stock_balances.comment: One row is an item in a store as it stands now: quantity in hand, reserved, free, value at the moving average rate, and the reorder level set for that store. Rows: every item that has had stock in the store (qty may be 0) or has a reorder level there. Quantities are in the store unit (unit), money in rupees. Use: stock value = sum(value), by store or category; what to reorder = below_reorder; items out of stock = qty = 0. Goods in transit between two stores are in no store until received. For stock on a past day or movement in a period use nlq.stock_ledger. Join nlq.stock_ledger or nlq.purchase_order_lines on item_id (and store_id for the ledger).

columns.name: store_id
columns.comment: Id of the store; join key to nlq.stock_ledger.store_id.

columns.name: store

columns.name: store_kind

columns.name: free_qty

columns.name: max_qty
columns.comment: Most the store should hold (store units); empty when not set.

columns.name: below_reorder
columns.comment: True when a reorder level above 0 is set and free_qty is at or below it.

nlq.stock_ledger.comment: One row is one move of an item into or out of a store: the stock ledger, never changed (a mistake is put right by another move). qty and value are signed: positive = into the store, negative = out of it. Quantities are in the store unit (unit), values in rupees at the moving average rate. Nothing is left out; instead is_internal marks moves that are not real stock in or out for the school: transfers between two stores (a pair, out of one store and into another; a cancelled transfer comes back into the same store), rate corrections (an out and an in of the same quantity) and openings that were reversed together with their reversal. Use: stock in or out in a period = filter moved_on and NOT is_internal, sum qty or value by kind; consumption = is_consumption (issues less goods returned unused), net = -sum(value), by department; stock of a store on a past day = sum(qty) and sum(value) of all moves (internal ones included) with moved_on up to that day. Goods enter on acceptance after inspection (kind receipt), not when they arrive. Stock now is nlq.stock_balances.

columns.name: department
columns.comment: Department the goods were issued to or came back from; empty for other kinds of move.

columns.name: other_store

columns.name: is_internal
columns.comment: True for moves that are not real stock in or out of the school: transfers between stores, rate corrections, reversed openings and their reversals. Leave them out of in/out totals; keep them for the stock of a store on a day.

columns.name: is_consumption
columns.comment: True for issues to departments and unused goods returned against them. -sum(qty) or -sum(value) of these rows is net consumption. Damaged goods brought back are not in the ledger, so they count as consumed here.

nlq.student_leaves.comment: One row is one leave application for a pupil, made by the family from the portal (or the office), with its type, dates, status and the pupil's class that year. Left out: the reason, certificates and approvers' notes; removed, merged or erased student records; pupils whose admission that year was cancelled. Leave asked through an older helpdesk "leave request" is not here. Days are calendar days (weekends and holidays included): days = as applied for; days_taken = days of an approved leave actually taken (a family may give up the rest: last_date stops the day before they came back). For "on leave today" use status = 'approved' AND from_date <= today AND last_date >= today. For school days of leave count is_leave in nlq.attendance_days instead. Filter by from_date (or month) and academic_year; group by class (sort class_order), leave_type_name or status.

columns.name: days

columns.name: days_taken
columns.comment: Calendar days of an approved leave actually taken (from_date to last_date); 0 for pending, rejected or cancelled leave.

columns.name: is_long
columns.comment: True for a long leave (more days than the school's limit), which needs more approval levels (class teacher, coordinator, principal by default).

columns.name: status

columns.name: ended_early

columns.name: applied_on

columns.name: decided_on

nlq.students.comment: One row is one pupil in one academic year: the class, section and roll number the pupil had that year (a pupil studying 5 years has 5 rows). Left out: cancelled enrolments (admissions cancelled as made by mistake), removed and merged duplicate student records, and records erased for data protection. Pupils who left stay, with enrolment_status withdrawn / transferred / left and ended_on. For "how many pupils now" or "strength of a class" filter is_current = true (counts each pupil once). For a past year filter academic_year and enrolment_status <> 'withdrawn' etc. as needed, or count those on roll on a date with joined_on <= date AND (ended_on IS NULL OR ended_on >= date). Always filter one academic year before counting, or a pupil is counted once per year. Group by class (sort by class_order), class_section, gender, category or house. Join other nlq views on student_id plus academic_year_id (the pupil's class in that year).

Cancelled admissions are not in this view.

columns.name: ended_on

nlq.teacher_subjects.comment: One row is one live teaching assignment: a teacher in a class section for a subject (subject teacher), or a role in the section without a subject (class teacher, co-class teacher, coordinator; indicator and remarks teachers may have one). Ended assignments are left out; a teacher who left keeps rows until the office ends them (see employee_is_current). Always filter one academic_year (e.g. the current one from nlq.academic_years where is_current). A teacher's periods are not here: one row per section and subject, not per period. nlq.term_results.comment: One row is one pupil's term or annual result (pupil × term code) as the class's result register (mark scheme) works it out from several exams (weightages, best of, conversions as the school set them) — the result the term and annual report cards print, promotion reads and the merit lists rank. Only registers in use: locked result registers not in the bin; one per class and term code. Stored rows, as of the register's last compute (computed_on); a register not computed yet has no rows. Left out: deleted, merged or erased pupils and cancelled enrolments. result: pass, compartment (failed a few subjects, up to the register's compartment limit), fail, absent (a blocking code such as AB in a counted subject: no total) or incomplete (marks missing: no total). Ranks are competition ranks (1, 2, 2, 4) among pass / compartment / fail rows. Subject-wise term marks are not in this view. Filter by term_code and academic_year; group by class (sort by class_order), class_section, result or division. Join nlq.students on (student_id, academic_year_id).

nlq.transport_riders.comment: One row is one pupil in one month they ride the school bus (pupil x month), taken from the approved transport periods. Left out: cancelled periods (never ran), months after the pupil left the school, removed and merged pupil records. For "how many pupils use the bus" count DISTINCT student_id for one month (filter month = a first-of-month date, or is_current_month = true); never sum rows across months as pupils. A pupil may ride one route in the morning (pick) and another in the afternoon (drop): for riders of a route on the morning trip filter pick_route_id = the route and rides_morning = true; on the afternoon trip drop_route_id and rides_afternoon; route_id is the main route (the pick route, else the drop route). monthly_amount is the transport rate of that month, not the bill: the fee actually billed and paid is in the fee views (transport head). Join nlq.transport_routes on route_id, nlq.students on student_id and academic_year_id.

The vehicle, driver and conductor are those that run the route today (from its dated vehicle mapping); a stand-in bus arranged for today is shown apart. Riders are the pupils on the route this month (India time), counted from the approved transport periods: morning_riders ride its morning (pick) trip, afternoon_riders its afternoon (drop) trip, riders either trip; a pupil can ride a different route each way, so do not add riders of several routes to get pupils - use nlq.transport_riders with count(DISTINCT student_id) for school totals. nlq.visitors.comment: One row is one visit through the school gate: a walk-in registered by the guard, a visitor who registered on their own phone and was let in, or an appointment visitor checked in (appointment visitors are already here — do not add appointments to these counts). Visitors who never came in (still waiting, refused or cancelled) are left out. No visitor name, mobile, ID proof, vehicle or photo is here. Count visits with count(*) and people with sum(people); filter and group by visit_on or month (India dates), purpose, visitor_type, host or host_employee_name, in_hour (busiest hours). inside_now = still inside (not checked out yet). minutes_inside is empty until they leave. Hostel visits to a boarder have hostel_visit = true and the boarder in the student columns.

columns.name: visit_id
columns.comment: The visit's id.

columns.name: number
columns.comment: The visitor pass number, e.g. V-2611-0042.

columns.name: visit_on
columns.comment: India date the visitor came in; the usual date to filter on.

columns.name: month
columns.comment: First day of the month of visit_on.

columns.name: in_time
columns.comment: India time the visitor came in, HH:MM (24-hour).

columns.name: in_hour
columns.comment: Hour of coming in, 0–23 (India time); group by it for the busiest hours.

columns.name: out_time
columns.comment: India time the visitor left, HH:MM; empty while inside.

columns.name: minutes_inside
columns.comment: Minutes between coming in and leaving; empty while inside. Use avg(minutes_inside).

columns.name: state
columns.comment: inside (not checked out yet) or left.

columns.name: inside_now
columns.comment: True when the visitor has not been checked out (still inside, or the guard forgot to check them out).

columns.name: source

columns.name: by_appointment

columns.name: purpose
columns.comment: Purpose of the visit from the school's list (e.g. Admission enquiry, Fees and accounts, Meet a teacher, Vendor or supplier, Official visit); anything typed by hand shows as Other.

columns.name: visitor_type

columns.name: people

columns.name: host

columns.name: host_kind

columns.name: host_employee_id

columns.name: host_employee_name

columns.name: gate

columns.name: exit_gate

columns.name: hostel_visit

columns.name: hostel

columns.name: warden_decision

columns.name: student_id

columns.name: admission_no
